title: Reading rhyme families like at, ig and op
examples: How do rhymes help me read?
What words are in the at family?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Which family does it belong to?

explain.say: Imagine a family where everyone has the same last name. Words have families too! Look at the board: cat, hat and mat all end the same way. They rhyme.

draw.text: Reading rhyme families like at, ig and op

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which family does it belong to?

explain.say: Look at the at family glowing. Every word ends with a and t. Only the first sound changes. If you can read cat, you can read hat, mat and sat. Can you read bat?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which family does it belong to?

explain.say: Now the ig family glows: pig, dig, big, wig. Cover the first letter with your finger and read the end. Then add the first sound back. Easy! Can you read fig?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which family does it belong to?

explain.say: Here comes the op family: hop, top, mop and shop. Hop like a bunny each time you read one! See how one word you know helps you read lots more?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which family does it belong to?

explain.say: You just read fourteen words by knowing three families. Wow! Your brain learns in its own way, and lots of brilliant people learn like this. Challenge: can you make a new word for the at family?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which family does it belong to?

faq.a: It is a group of words that end with the same letters and sound, like cat, hat and mat. Only the first sound changes.
asks: Tell me about the at family

faq.q: How do rhyme families help me read?
faq.a: Once you know the ending, you only need to change the first sound. One word you know unlocks lots of new words.

faq.q: How do I read a new word in a family?
faq.a: Cover the first letter and read the ending. Then add the first sound and blend them together.
asks: Tell me about the ig family

faq.q: Do all rhyming words look the same?
faq.a: Not always. Blue and shoe rhyme, but they end with different letters. Families with the same letters are the easiest place to start.
asks: Do rhymes always end the same?

faq.q: What games can I play with rhyme families?
faq.a: Try a rhyme chain: say cat, then hat, mat and sat. A teacher or grown-up can make letter cards so you can swap the first letter.
asks: Tell me about the op family

facts: Cat, hat, mat and sat share the ending at, so they rhyme.
Some words rhyme but are spelled differently, like blue and shoe.

quiz.say: Which word belongs to the ig family?
quiz.show: Which word is in the ig family?
quiz.why: Wig ends with i and g, just like pig and dig.

wrong.1: Wag ends with a and g, so it is in the ag family.
wrong.2: Web ends with e and b.

quiz.say: If you can read hop, which word is easy to read next?
quiz.show: You can read hop. Which is easy next?
quiz.why: Top is in the op family, just like hop. Only the first sound changes.

wrong.1: Hip changes the middle sound, so it is in the ip family.
wrong.2: Hat is in the at family.
